cur-fossil-callabonna.dateNote: In 1892 a stockman, Frederick Ragless, found giant bones in this dry salt lake in South Australia. In 1893 Edward Stirling and Amandus Zietz dug out whole Diprotodon skeletons. They are Ice Age bones, well under 1 million years old.
cur-fossil-callabonna.summary: A dry lake where dozens of Diprotodons were found stuck in the mud where they died.

cur-fossil-lark-quarry.dateNote: Dug out in 1976–77 by volunteers led by the Queensland Museum: about 3,300 footprints of small dinosaurs, long read as a "stampede", now often as a river crossing. The sandstone is about 95 million years old (Winton Formation, Late Cretaceous).

cur-fossil-winton.dateNote: In 1999 David Elliott, mustering sheep on Belmont Station near Winton, found part of a giant sauropod thigh bone. More finds followed, and in 2002 he set up a museum. The Winton Formation is about 95 million years old (Late Cretaceous). Pinned at the Australian Age of Dinosaurs museum, outside Winton.
cur-fossil-winton.summary: Where a sheep farmer's find in 1999 started Australia's dinosaur rush.
